metadata.title: Rising Tides: CMIP6 Regional Sea Level Projections

ssp126.name: SSP1-2.6 (Paris Agreement)
ssp126.desc: Aggressive decarbonization limiting warming to ~1.5°C - 2.0°C by 2100.

ssp585.name: SSP5-8.5 (Worst-Case)
ssp585.desc: Unconstrained fossil-fueled development; global temperatures rise >4.0°C.

global.name: Global Ocean Overview
global.driver: Thermal expansion of seawater + melting glaciers and ice sheets (Greenland & Antarctica).

east-coast.name: US East Coast
east-coast.driver: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) slowdown pushes water onto the coast, combined with post-glacial land subsidence.

gulf-coast.name: US Gulf of Mexico
gulf-coast.driver: Severe local land subsidence from sediment compaction and fluid extraction amplifies global rise into the fastest relative sea level rise in North America.

west-coast.name: US West Coast
west-coast.driver: Steep rocky topography mitigates total acreage lost, but low-lying bays (SF Bay, Puget Sound) and coastal bluff erosion face acute storm-surge hazards during El Niño.

hawaii.name: Hawaii & Central Pacific
hawaii.driver: Island communities depend on narrow coastal plains where Waikiki and airport runways sit mere inches above king tides, threatening groundwater tables and reef ecosystems.

bangladesh.name: Bangladesh & Bay of Bengal
bangladesh.driver: A low-lying mega-delta housing over 160 million people. Rising tides penetrate miles inland, salinizing rice fields and displacing entire coastal fishing communities.

pacific-atolls.name: Pacific Atolls (Tuvalu & Kiribati)
pacific-atolls.driver: Maximum elevations barely 2-3 meters above mean sea level. Sea water seeps up from porous coral foundations, destroying freshwater lenses and making nations physically uninhabitable.

conclusion.name: Global Synthesis: The Divergence
conclusion.driver: The difference between SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 is not just numbers—it is hundreds of coastal cities, millions of displaced climate refugees, and entire sovereign nations.
